statement: A glass elevator starts at a height of $96$ meters and descends at a constant rate. Its height, in meters, $t$ seconds after it starts is given by $h(t) = 96 - 3t$. How many seconds after it starts is the elevator at a height of $39$ meters?

choices.misconception: I divided the target height, 39, by the rate of 3 and got 13, instead of first finding how far the elevator has to fall.
I found how long it takes to reach the ground, $96 \div 3 = 32$, instead of how long it takes to reach 39 meters.
I added 39 to 96 instead of subtracting, so I got $135 \div 3 = 45$.

hints: Solve $96 - 3t = 39$ by moving the constant to one side and then dividing.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
